translation.title: Quraysh
notes: English translation added as 'text_en' (segments, footnotes), 'lemma_en' (lemma headings) and '*_en' metadata fields; all original Arabic fields are unchanged. Segment boundaries follow the printed pages, so some sentences are split across segments. Qur'anic quotations are rendered in translation; transliterated reading variants are given in parentheses.

x: Commentary on the Surah "Quraysh". In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
On the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted, whose names are sanctified:
For the accustoming (ilaf) of Quraysh (1) their accustomed journey in winter and summer (2) Let them worship the Lord of this House (3) Who fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear (4)
. The reciters differed in how they read
. The general body of the reciters of the major centers read it with a ya after the hamza:
, except Abu Ja'far, who agreed on
, reading it with a ya after the hamza, but about whom there are differing reports regarding
: it is reported from him that he read it (ilfihim), as a verbal noun from "alifa, ya'lafu, alfan", without a ya
. Some have also related from him that he read it (ilafihim) without a ya, with a short alif. The correct reading in this, in my view, is that of those who read
with the ya retained in both after the hamza, from "alaftu al-shay' ulifuhu ilafan", because the authoritative reciters are agreed on it

The Arabs have two dialects for this: "alaftu" and "alifto". Whoever says "alaftu", with the alif lengthened, says: "I am ulifu, ilafan"; and whoever says "alifto", with the alif shortened, says: "I am alafu, ilfan", and he is a man who is "alif" (inclined to familiarity), ilfan
. It is reported of 'Ikrimah that he used to read this as (li-ya'laf
Abu Kurayb related that to me, saying:

c: Waki' related to us, from Abu Makin,
m: . Something has also been reported from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, on this, as Ibn Humayd related to us, saying:

c: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid, who said:
m: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, read: (ilfihim rihlata al-shita'i wa-l-sayf)

x: The people of Arabic differed over the meaning that brings in this lam in His saying:
. One of the grammarians of Basra used to say: What brings it in is His saying:
and He made them like eaten straw
[al-Fil (printed "al-Qil"): 5]. So, according to this speaker, it is connected to His saying

: "He made them". On this view the meaning of the passage must be: We did that to the Companions of the Elephant as a favor from Us to the people of this House and a kindness from Us to them, in addition to Our favor to them in the winter and summer journey. So the lam in
would mean "to" (ila), as if it were said: a favor upon a favor, and in addition to a favor, because "ila" can stand in the place of the lam, and the lam in the place of "ila".
Some of the people of interpretation have also given a meaning to this effect.
Mention of those who said that: * Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying:

c: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Waraqa' related to us,
m: all together from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, on His saying:
their accustomed journey in winter and summer
. He said: Their being accustomed to that, so that no journey in winter or summer is hard on them

c: Isma'il ibn Musa al-Suddi related to me, saying: Sharik informed us, from Ibrahim ibn al-Muhajir, from Mujahid:
m: . He said: My favor upon Quraysh.

c: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hilali related to me, saying: Farwah ibn Abi al-Maghra' al-Kindi related to us, saying: Sharik related to us, from Ibrahim ibn al-Muhajir, from Mujahid,

'Amr ibn 'Ali related to us, saying: 'Amir ibn Ibrahim al-Isbahani related to us, saying: Khattab ibn Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah related to us, saying: My father related to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas,
m: . He said: My favor upon Quraysh
. One of the grammarians of Kufa

used to say: This view has been put forward, and it is also said that He, blessed and exalted, expressed wonder to His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saying: Marvel, Muhammad, at God's favors upon Quraysh in their accustoming their journey in winter and summer. Then He said: So let them not be distracted by that from faith in God and from following you. He draws this from His saying:
Let them worship the Lord of this House
. And some of the people of interpretation [direct the interpretation of this toward the view we mentioned from some of the Basrans, except that he]
directs the interpretation of His saying
to their familiarity with one another.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying:
m: Ibn Zayd said, on His saying:
Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the Companions of the Elephant

[al-Fil: 1] to the end of the surah. He said: This is the ilaf of Quraysh; I did this to them for the familiarity of Quraysh, so that I would not break up their familiarity and their unity. The master of the elephant came only to destroy their sanctuary, and God did that to him

. The soundest of the views on this in my opinion is to say: this lam carries the sense of wonder, and the meaning of the passage is: Marvel at the ilaf of Quraysh, their journey of winter and summer, and their abandonment of the worship of the Lord of this House, Who fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear

. When the Arabs bring in this lam and place it in speech to express wonder, they treat it as sufficient indication of wonder without stating the verb that would bring it, as the poet said: "Does it delude you that they called Qurrah a poet? Oh, how wondrous is his father, as a tribe-chief and poet!" so the lam was taken as sufficient indication of wonder, in place of stating the verb. The speech is really: "Does it delude you that they said ... Marvel at Qurrah as a poet!" The same holds for His saying:
. As for the view of the one whose statement we have reported, that it is connected to His saying
and He made them like eaten straw
would have to be part of
, and it would not be a surah separate from
. The consensus of all Muslims that they are two complete surahs, each separate from
the other, shows the falsity of what the one who said that has said. And if His saying
and He made them like eaten straw
* would not be complete until it was joined to His saying
, because speech is not complete until the report that was mentioned is finished.

x: The people of interpretation have spoken in line with what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas,
m: on His saying: (ilfihim rihlata al-shita'i wa-l-sayf). He says: Their attachment to it

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas,
m: . He said: He forbade them the journey and commanded them to worship the Lord of this House, and spared them the burden. Their journey was in winter and summer, so they had no rest in winter or summer; so after that He fed them against hunger, and made them safe from fear, and they became used to travelling: when they wished they set out, and when they wished they stayed. That was among God's favors to them.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Dawud related to us, from 'Ikrimah, who said:
m: Quraysh had become accustomed to Busra and Yemen; they went back and forth to the one in winter and to the other in summer.
So let them worship the Lord of this House
: so He commanded them to stay in Mecca

c: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih:
m: . He said: They were merchants, so God knew their love of Syria

c: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah:
m: . He said: The habit of Quraysh; their habit was the journey of winter and summer

c: It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said:
m: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, on His saying:
: They had become accustomed to travelling in the summer heat and in winter.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in how they read {li-ilafi Quraysh (1) ilafihim}.

The general body of the reciters of the major centers read it with a ya after the hamza: {li-ilafi} and {ilafihim}, except Abu Ja'far, who agreed on {li-ilafi}, reading it with a ya after the hamza, but about whom there are differing reports regarding {ilafihim}: it is reported from him that he read it (ilfihim), as a verbal noun from "alifa, ya'lafu, alfan", without a ya (1).
Some have also related from him that he read it (ilafihim) without a ya, with a short alif.

The correct reading in this, in my view, is that of those who read {li-ilafi Quraysh ilafihim} with the ya retained in both after the hamza, from "alaftu al-shay' ulifuhu ilafan", because the authoritative reciters are agreed on it (2).
It is reported of 'Ikrimah that he used to read this as (li-ya'laf (1) Quraysh ilfahum rihlata al-shita'i wa-l-sayf).

x: . It is in the genitive as a substitution (badal), as if He had said: for the ilaf of Quraysh, for their ilaf, the journey of winter and summer. As for "the journey" (al-rihlah), it is in the accusative because of His saying
their journey in winter and summer
. He says: the journey of Quraysh, the two journeys; one of them to Syria in summer, and the other to Yemen in winter.

c: Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying:
m: Ibn Zayd said, on His saying:
their journey in winter and summer
. He said: They had two journeys: in summer to Syria, and in winter to Yemen, for trade. When winter came, Syria was closed to them because of the cold, so their winter journey was to Yemen

c: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan:
m: their journey in winter and summer

c: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Kalbi:
m: their journey in winter and summer
. He said: They had two journeys: a journey in winter to Yemen, and a journey in summer to Syria

c: 'Amr ibn 'Ali related to us, saying: 'Amir ibn Ibrahim al-Isbahani related to us, saying: Khattab ibn Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah related to us, saying: My father related to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas:
m: their accustomed journey in winter and summer
. He said: They would spend the winter in Mecca and the summer in al-Ta'if

x: Let them worship the Lord of this House
. He says: let them stay in their place and homeland of Mecca and worship the Lord of this House. By "the House" He means the Ka'bah.

c: As Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim,
m: that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, prayed the Maghrib prayer in Mecca and recited:
; and when he reached His saying
Let them worship the Lord of this House
, he pointed with his hand to the House

c: 'Amr ibn 'Ali related to us, saying: 'Amir ibn Ibrahim al-Isbahani related to us, saying: Khattab ibn Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah related to us, saying: My father related to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas,
m: Let them worship the Lord of this House

x: Some of them said: They were commanded to become accustomed to the worship of the Lord of Mecca, as they were accustomed to the two journeys.
Mention of those who said that:

c: 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid al-Amuli related to us, saying: Marwan related to us, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas,
m: . He said: They were commanded to become accustomed to the worship of the Lord of this House, as they were accustomed to the journey of winter and summer

x: . He says: Who fed Quraysh against hunger.

c: As 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas,
m: : he means Quraysh, the people of Mecca, through the prayer of Abraham, peace be upon him, when he said:
and made them safe from fear

x: The people of interpretation differed over the meaning of His saying
and made them safe from fear

Some of them said: the meaning is that He made them safe from what is feared by those who are not people of the Sanctuary: raids, wars and fighting, and the things of which the Arabs feared one another.
Mention of those who said that:

c: 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas:
m: and made them safe from fear
: when Abraham, peace be upon him, said:
My Lord, make this a secure land

c: Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Waraqa' related to us,
m: all together from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, His saying:
and made them safe from fear
. He said: He made them safe from every enemy in their Sanctuary

c: Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah,
m: . He said: The people of Mecca were merchants, who went back and forth

in winter and summer, safe among the Arabs, while the Arabs raided one another and could not do so to them, being unable out of fear, to the point that a man of them might be caught in one of the tribes of the Arabs, and when it was said "a Harami (man of the Sanctuary)", he and his property were left alone, in reverence for the security God had given them

c: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah:
m: and made them safe from fear
. He said: They used to say: We are of God's Sanctuary. So no one interfered with them in the Jahiliyyah; they were safe by that, whereas others of the Arab tribes were raided when they went out

c: Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying:
m: Ibn Zayd said, on His saying:
and made them safe from fear
. He said: The Arabs raided one another and took one another captive, and they were made safe from that because of the Sanctuary. And he recited:
Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary to which are brought the fruits of all things

x: Others said: What is meant is: and He made them safe from leprosy (judham).
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Harith related to us, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Waraqa' related to us, saying: al-Dahhak said:
m: and made them safe from fear
. He said: From their fear of leprosy

c: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying:
m: and made them safe from fear
. He said: From leprosy and other things

c: Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' said:
m: , to him. He said: The hunger;
and made them safe from fear

c: 'Amr ibn 'Ali related to us, saying: 'Amir ibn Ibrahim al-Isbahani related to us, saying: Khattab ibn Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah related to us, saying: My father related to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas:
m: and made them safe from fear
. He said: The fear is leprosy

. The correct position on this is to say: God, mighty be His mention, informed that He made them safe from fear; and the enemy is something feared, and leprosy is something feared, and God did not restrict the report to His having made them safe from the enemy and not from leprosy, nor from leprosy and not from the enemy, but made the report general. So the correct course is to take it as general, as He, glorified be His mention, made it general, and to say: He made them safe from both meanings. End of the commentary on Surat Quraysh.

notes.en: Ibn ʿAmir read the word without a yāʾ after the hamza (liʾilaf), like liʿilaf. Abu Jaʿfar read it with a quiescent yāʾ and no hamza (li-yilaf), while the others read it with a kasra on the hamza followed by a quiescent yāʾ (li-ilaf). They also differed over “their ilaf”: Abu Jaʿfar read it with a kasra on the hamza and no yāʾ; this is also the reading of ʿIkrima, Shayba, and Ibn ʿUtba, and is also reported from Ibn Kathir. See al-Nashr (2/302) and Ithaf Fudalaʾ al-Bashar (p. 274).
notes.ar: قرأ ابن عامر بغير ياء بعد الهمزة (لئلاف) مثل (لعِلاف)، وقرأ أبو جعفر بياء ساكنة من غير همزة (ليلاف)، وقرأ الباقون بهمزة مكسورة بعدها ياء ساكنة (لإيلاف)، واختلفوا في (إيلافهم) فقرأ أبو جعفر بهمزة مكسورة من غير ياء، وهى قراءة عكرمة وشيبة وابن عتبة، وجاءت عن ابن كثير أيضًا. ينظر النشر 2/ 302، وإتحاف فضلاء البشر ص 274.

notes.en: The readings of Ibn ʿAmir and Abu Jaʿfar (liʾilaf and li-yilaf) are mutawatir, as is Abu Jaʿfar’s reading of “ilafahum.”
notes.ar: قراءة ابن عامر وأبي جعفر (لئِلاف)، (ليلاف) متواترة، وكذلك قراءة أبي جعفر (إلافهم) متواترة أيضًا.

notes.en: Manuscript M reads “li-taʾlaf.” See Mukhtasar Shawadh al-Qurʾan by Ibn Khalawayh (p. 181). Abu Hayyan says in al-Bahr al-Muhit (8/514): another reading from him is “li-taʾlaf Quraysh,” as a command; from him and Hilal ibn Fityan it is also reported with the lām of command opened.
notes.ar: في م: "لتألف". وينظر مختصر الشواذ لابن خالويه ص 181، وقال أبو حيان في البحر المحيط 8/ 514: وعنه أيضًا: لتألف قريش. على الأمر، وعنه وعن هلال بن فتيان بفتح لام الأمر.

notes.en: Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/397) to the author.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 397 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: Abu ʿAmr al-Duri transmitted it in a treatise on the Prophet’s recitation (no. 123), and Ibn Abi Hatim in his Tafsir—as cited in Ibn Kathir’s Tafsir (8/513)—and al-Tabarani (24/177–178, no. 447) through Sufyan. Al-Hakim transmitted it (2/256) through Shahr. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/397) to al-Firyabi and Ibn Mardawayh. This is an anomalous reading.
notes.ar: أخرجه أبو عمرو الدورى في جزء فيه قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم (123)، وابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره - كما في تفسير ابن كثير 8/ 513 - والطبراني 24/ 177، 178 (447) من طريق سفيان به، وأخرجه الحاكم 2/ 256 من طريق شهر به وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 397 إلى الفريابي وابن مردويه. والقراءة شاذة.

notes.ar: في ص، ت 2، ت 3: "إيلاف".

notes.en: Manuscripts S, T1, T2, and T3 read “li-qawlihim.”

notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 752 ومن طريقه الفريابي - كما في التغليق 4/ 377 - وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 397 إلى ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Al-Nasaʾi transmitted it in al-Sunan al-Kubra (no. 11699), and al-Nahhas—as cited in al-Qurtubi’s Tafsir (20/201)—from ʿAmr ibn ʿAli with this chain. Ibn Mardawayh transmitted it—as cited in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/397)—and through him al-Diyaʾ in al-Mukhtara (nos. 125–126), through ʿAmir ibn Ibrahim. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/397) to Ibn Abi Hatim.
notes.ar: أخرجه النَّسَائِي في الكبرى (11699)، وعنه النحاس - كما في تفسير القرطبي 20/ 201 - عن عمرو بن علي به، وأخرجه ابن مردويه - كما في الدر المنثور 6/ 397 - ومن طريقه الضياء في (125، 126) من طريق عامر بن إبراهيم به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 397 إلى ابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Ibn Mardawayh transmitted it in his Tafsir—as cited in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/397)—and through him al-Diyaʾ in al-Mukhtara (nos. 125–126), through ʿAmir ibn Ibrahim. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur to Ibn Abi Hatim.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن مردويه في تفسيره - كما في الدر المنثور 6/ 397 - ومن طريقه الضياء في المختارة (125، 126) من طريق عامر بن إبراهيم به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور إلى ابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/398) to the author.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 398 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzaq transmitted it in his Tafsir (2/398) from Maʿmar with this chain. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/398) to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 398 عن معمر به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 398 إلى ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.
